title: Transparent degraded-mode bridge and persistent metric guard
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: production incidents in the last quarter exposed two correlated issues: (1) regional controllers reopened circuits too aggressively after transient KV pressure spikes causing flapping; (2) telemetry-based SLO detectors could be starved during short draining windows and emit false positives which triggered preemptive failovers. This PR introduces a lightweight 'degraded-mode bridge' in the runtime control plane that coordinates a graceful transition into degraded mode across regions and a 'persistent metric guard' that prevents short-lived telemetry noise from causing circuit state churn.

What this changes: single-string summary of changes (see files_changed below). Key behavioral updates: the bridge establishes an ephemeral lease between local and regional controllers when a node requests soft-evac; during the lease the system enforces a gentle KV drain window extension and successively softer backoff on reopen attempts. The persistent metric guard adds a small sliding-window counter with hysteresis for SLO breach metrics used by the failover decision path.

Compatibility/rollout: guarded behind a runtime feature flag redwood.degraded_bridge.v1 and an operator config in configs/defaults.yaml. Default behaviour remains unchanged. We will rollout to canary region for 48 hours, verify SLO and circuit-stability metrics, then ramp to 50% and finally global.

Testing: unit tests for metric guard logic and lease reconciliation added; an integration canary test simulating KV pressure and short reconnects was added to perf-canary. Manual verification done on staging region-east.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-2145
- [x] Unit tests (runtime + metrics)
- [x] Integration canary job
- [x] Telemetry dashboards + alerts updated (see release_notes)
- [x] Feature flag + operator config present

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids aggressive global circuit resets; instead it prefers local extension and coordinated gradual reopen. The change is conservative and intended to reduce tenant-visible flapping while preserving fast recovery when underlying resources stabilize.

release_notes:
- Introduced a transparent degraded-mode bridge to coordinate soft-evacuations and reduce circuit reopen flapping.
- Added persistent metric guard that reduces false-positive SLO alerts during short KV pressure spikes.
- Configurable region overrides for drain windows and reopen backoff.
- New operator playbook for degraded-mode rollouts.
Impact: improves circuit stability and reduces unnecessary regional failovers; opt-in via feature flag; rollout plan in PR description.
